references.text: God punishes those who hate him, to the third and fourth generation, which reflects the theme of retribution against those who hate God.
The Lord will by no means leave the guilty unpunished, emphasizing God's righteous judgment on sinners.
The Lord is slow to anger, but he will not leave the guilty unpunished. This expresses the same principle of God's righteous retribution.
The Lord will make them a burning furnace on his day of wrath and consume them, showing God's judgment over his enemies.
God repays according to deeds: wrath to his adversaries and punishment to his foes.
The Lord takes vengeance on his adversaries and keeps anger against his enemies.
Paul writes about God's righteous judgment that repays each person according to their deeds, which aligns with the principle in Deuteronomy.
Vengeance belongs to the Lord, and he will repay. This confirms God's sovereign right to judge and punish.
The Lord will judge his people, and it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. This underscores God's direct and immediate judgment.
